therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: adults with manic or mixed episode of Bipolar I Disorder
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline to 3-week endpoint in YMRS total score

results.effect_size: Least Squares Mean Difference vs placebo = -5.62 (95% CI: -8.87 to -2.37) on YMRS total score at 3 weeks
subgroup_findings: Haloperidol showed greater YMRS reduction at 3 weeks (-14.3) vs olanzapine (-12.6) vs placebo (-6.8)
At 6 weeks, olanzapine and haloperidol showed similar YMRS reductions (-16.0 vs -14.7); no significant difference (p=0.774)
Bipolar disorder remission rate at 6 weeks: olanzapine 44.2% vs haloperidol 20.0% (p=0.064)
Haloperidol showed higher rates of symptomatic depression switch at 3 and 6 weeks (16.7%) vs olanzapine (2.4%)
Haloperidol showed significantly greater extrapyramidal symptoms (DIEPSS max change 2.70 vs olanzapine 0.70, p=0.003)
safety_signals: Haloperidol associated with significantly higher drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms (DIEPSS max change 2.70 vs 0.70 for olanzapine, p=0.003)
Haloperidol associated with higher rates of symptomatic depression switch (16.7% vs 2.4% for olanzapine at 6 weeks, p=0.014)
Serious adverse events: status epilepticus (placebo 1/96), bipolar I disorder (olanzapine 1/105, placebo 1/96), mania (placebo 1/96)

dose_info.schedule: olanzapine once daily (evening); haloperidol twice daily (morning and evening); placebo twice daily
